purpose: Curated plant-health evidence registry for dr-plant. Records are references and research leads, not diagnostic training labels unless explicitly validated.

rules.promotion: A finding may be used as diagnostic evidence only after expert review, symptom verification, image provenance and license checks.
rules.socialMedia: Social-media posts are leads only. Never treat captions or comments as confirmed diagnoses.
rules.images: Do not copy or redistribute images until their license or explicit permission is verified.
rules.uncertainty: Keep suspected, reported, and confirmed findings separate.

diseases.notes: Differential-diagnosis reference. A 2025 study from Sweida in southern Syria reported isolation of Phomopsis viticola from symptomatic grapevine samples collected during 2020–2022; confirm current accepted taxonomy and local coastal occurrence separately. This is Syrian evidence, but not evidence from Latakia or Tartous.

diseases.notes: A peer-reviewed first report documented a 2006 survey and serological testing in Syrian citrus-growing areas including Jableh and other locations in Latakia, and sites in Tartous. Treat this as a historical published regional record, not a statement about present-day prevalence or any particular tree. Symptoms alone are insufficient; laboratory testing is required.

diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead; location and season were not specified. Extension references describe feeding damage as fine yellow/white stippling, progressing to bronzing or necrosis; webbing may be present with web-spinning species such as Tetranychus urticae but is not universal across mites. Confirm mites on the leaf underside with magnification; distinguish pest mites from predatory mites. Do not identify species from leaf color alone.

diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead; location and season were not specified. Thrips can injure emerging shoots and young leaves; some species cause leaf cupping or distortion, while feeding on fruit may cause scarring. Symptoms vary by species, vine stage and cultivar. Treat as an insect-pest differential, not a fungal disease; verify the insect or characteristic feeding injury before assigning a diagnosis.

sources.title: UC IPM – Thrips on Grape

commonNames: اصفرار أوراق العنب بسبب نقص العناصر
diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead; location and season were not specified. Yellowing is a symptom, not a nutrient diagnosis. Nitrogen deficiency may cause general paling/yellowing; magnesium commonly causes interveinal chlorosis on older/basal leaves; potassium can cause interveinal or marginal chlorosis and later scorching. Patterns overlap with water stress, root problems, disease and other disorders. Do not recommend a specific nutrient from a photograph alone; use soil/petiole or tissue analysis and field context.

diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead; location and season were not specified. Larvae mine within young expanding leaves, creating narrow serpentine/silvery galleries, often with a visible frass line; leaves may curl or become distorted. Chlorosis can occur in damaged tissue. Diagnose from the characteristic winding mine rather than yellowing alone. The pest attacks citrus generally, including lemon.

sources.title: UF/IFAS – Citrus Leafminer Pest Quick Guide
UC IPM – Citrus: Identifying Diseases and Disorders of Leaves and Twigs

diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead; location and season were not specified. Yellowing is a nonspecific symptom and must not be treated as one disease. Possible causes include nitrogen, iron, zinc or magnesium deficiency, waterlogging or drought, salinity, root dysfunction, mites and infectious disease. The pattern and age of affected leaves help narrow the differential, but laboratory/soil/tissue tests and field context may be needed. Do not label a nutrient deficiency from color alone.

diseases.scientificName: Venturia oleaginea (syn. Spilocaea oleagina; anamorph name)
diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead; location, cultivar, season, specimen and expert confirmation were not specified. Typical symptoms are circular brown/olive-green to gray or dark spots, often with concentric rings and a yellow halo, mainly on the upper leaf surface. Severe/recurrent infection can cause chlorosis and premature leaf fall, especially in humid lower canopy. Infection is favored by prolonged leaf wetness, rain/high humidity and mild temperatures. Some infections may remain latent for months; absence of visible spots does not exclude infection. Do not diagnose from yellowing alone; microscopy or suitable laboratory testing can confirm.

datasets.name: HERMOS grape disease dataset
datasets.intendedUse: Candidate for research; inspect annotation format, provenance and class balance before training.
datasets.notes: Original HERMOS publication reports 492 images and 13,913 Pascal VOC annotations from western Anatolia, Turkey. A 2026 CC BY 4.0 study reports retaining 491 source images and 13,765 regions after its own audit/filtering. Treat 491/13,765 as the independently reported filtered subset in that study, not necessarily a replacement official release count. Audit the downloaded version, labels, duplicates, and archive before training. Important count discrepancy: the Mendeley V2 landing page currently displays 914 images/13,904 labels, whereas the original 2022 paper states 492 images/13,913 labels and the 2026 audit found 492 image/XML pairs, 13,904 parsed objects, 13,765 usable regions, and 491 retained source images. These figures are not interchangeable; inspect the actual downloaded archive before using any count or manifest.
datasets.licenseEvidence: A 2026 peer-reviewed open-access study explicitly identifies HERMOS Mendeley Version 2 as CC BY 4.0; still preserve attribution and verify the downloaded version and file provenance.

datasets.notes: The peer-reviewed Data in Brief article provides detailed provenance and collection dates. Data came from four northern-Portugal vineyard sites over 2024–2025. Keep site/date groups together in the holdout split; the same-site/time random split used in the paper may overstate transfer to new vineyards. Not Syrian coastal evidence.
